verdicts.stemStart: Mas de Valériole ‘Vé’ magnum, region: Camargue, near Arles, France
verdicts.why: The original was true but out of form, and it resolved to France alone; the new string resolves to the Provence article (regions-join, exact) and changes no Terroir row. Gageron lies in the commune of Arles, in the Grande Camargue of the Bouches-du-Rhône, so Provence is right for this estate even though the Petite Camargue reaches into the Gard. The string claims no Provence appellation; the IGP stays in the wine’s name, and the IGP question is filed as an ask.

verdicts.stemStart: Jean Foillard ‘Côte du Py’ magnum, region: Morgon, Beaujolais, France
verdicts.why: Not wrong before, but the same wine in bottle and every other Beaujolais card carry Burgundy, and a magnum should not read as a different place. The join resolves Beaujolais either way; the one side effect is that the recite call The Morgon, Beaujolais, France pour, a near twin of the bottle’s, is no longer dealt, which is a gain.

verdicts.stemStart: Jean-Philippe Fichet Bourgogne Blanc 2023, region: Meursault, Côte de Beaune
verdicts.why: The fix is right: the appellation is Bourgogne. The reason was not: no TERROIR row at any level is named Meursault, and regions-join resolves both the old and the new string to Burgundy, so the card never linked a Meursault Terroir row. What misled was the Region line the card prints, identical to the village Meursaults’. Reason rewritten to say so, and the batch note’s section 3 added to the source; the same false Terroir claim stands in the note’s header and section 3 for the integrator to strike.

verdicts.stemStart: Domaine Coche-Dury Bourgogne Blanc 2022, region: Meursault, Côte de Beaune
verdicts.why: As for Fichet: the to-text is right and introduces only Bourgogne, from the wine’s own name; the reason’s Terroir row claim was false and is replaced by the printed Region line, and section 4 of the batch note is added to the source.

verdicts.stemStart: Château d’Esclans ‘Whispering Angel’, region: Côtes de Provence, France
verdicts.why: A form fix, not an error fix: the old string was true and resolved to Provence already. It brings the card into line with Bandol and Alpilles and changes nothing a server is taught, so it stands as harmless consistency.

verdicts.stemStart: Loimer ‘Lois’ Grüner Veltliner 2022, region: Kamptal, Austria
verdicts.why: Kept in substance: a search of my own (11 October 2026) found Delectable listing the 2022 as Lois Niederösterreich and a Wine Spectator review of the 2009 printing Qualitätswein Niederösterreich Lois, so the generic region is the Lois’s long-standing label; Champion’s Niederösterreich DAC is not a real DAC and is rightly not used. The reason was tightened: across Lower Austria overstated the one summary that says in Lower Austria, and the Kamptal was called not the wine’s appellation when Niederösterreich is not an appellation either. The join and the producer grouping are unchanged; Delectable also lists a 2023 as Lois Kamptal, so the filed label ask still matters for later vintages.

verdicts.stemStart: Loimer ‘Lois’ profile: A light, fresh Grüner Veltliner from the Kamptal:
verdicts.why: True whichever the label prints, in the voice, British in its spelling, and Lower Austria is the English form of the Niederösterreich the note sources. parts.main (Langenlois in the Kamptal) still contradicts it and is set down for the integrator in the note.

verdicts.stemStart: Stein ‘Weihwasser’ profile: from old vines on steep slate near the old church in Alf:
verdicts.why: A second search of my own (11 October 2026) found retailers agreeing on the St. Aldegunder Klosterkammer, steep blue slate and vines near an old church, but giving fifty to sixty year old vines unevenly and placing the church in Alf for a site named after St. Aldegund, so the original was a retailer’s slip carried as fact. The to-text keeps only the steep slate, which those pages and the producer profile support. Still carrying the unsettled place and vine age, outside this batch’s fields: the s45 (for its old vines near the village church), the compare row (from old vines at Alf), parts.main and parts.technique and kept notes 2 and 3.

verdicts.stemStart: Chateau Montelena Chardonnay Napa Valley 2023, region: Calistoga, Napa Valley
verdicts.why: The fix only removes a place no current source gives the Chardonnay and leaves the appellation the wine’s own name prints; Napa Valley, California is true wherever in the valley the fruit grows. The join and the Terroir row (Napa Valley) are unchanged.

verdicts.stemStart: Pascal Cotat ‘Lot 2024’ Chavignol Rosé, region: Chavignol, Sancerre, Loire
verdicts.why: The rosé is Vin de France by the sourced card, and Sancerre standing in the string as an appellation contradicted the card’s own warning; the to-text introduces no name. The join resolves Loire either way. The Monts Damnés keeps the Sancerre string, so the two Chavignol calls in the recite deck now teach the difference rather than collapse into one.
